title: Flaky Roti Canai with Coiled Buttery Layers
summary: Golden, flaky flatbread built from countless paper-thin layers, pan-fried until crisp outside and soft within, perfect for mopping up a curry.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
neutral oil, plus extra for greasing and frying

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Combine 330 g plain flour, 87 g '00' flour and 2 tsp fine salt in a mixer bowl.

steps.title: Knead
steps.text: Whisk 1 egg, 78 g condensed milk and 175 ml warm water into the flour and knead on low until soft and smooth, 8-10 min, then rest covered for 30 min.

steps.title: Coat
steps.text: Divide into 6 balls, roll smooth, coat each in a mix of 35 g softened butter and 3 tbsp oil, then rest covered at room temperature for at least 4 h.

steps.title: Stretch
steps.text: Oil the worktop and stretch each ball into a paper-thin sheet about 50 cm across, brushing with a little fat.

steps.title: Coil
steps.text: Fold the edges inward into a rope, coil into a snail and tuck the end under, then rest 30-60 min covered.

steps.title: Flatten
steps.text: Press each coil out to a 20 cm round.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Cook each roti in a lightly oiled pan over medium heat for 2-3 min per side until golden and crisp in spots.

steps.title: Fluff
steps.text: Stack 2-3 hot roti and scrunch between your palms to loosen the layers before serving.

tips: Keep your hands and worktop well oiled so the dough stretches paper-thin without tearing too much.
Give the coated dough balls the full resting time so the layers separate easily when stretched.
Clap or scrunch the cooked roti straight from the pan to fluff up the layers before serving.
storage: Best eaten hot and fresh from the pan; any leftovers can be kept covered for a day and reheated in a dry pan to crisp them back up. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
